gloss: to gaze toward · hope · the full moon
formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿱⿰亡𱼀𡈼 (from the database, 2026-11-05). This describes the graph’s parts, not its history; the etymology is not yet researched.
summary: To look into the distance, and so to hope; also the full moon, when moon and sun face each other.
placement: Chosen by farthest-point sampling on the integrated Lorenz-84 trajectory, so the eight stars spread across its projected shape. 望 takes the highest point, gazing up; 劫 the point farthest from the rest, at the edge of the eon. A design choice, not a claim.

satellites.title: On Tiptoe, Looking Toward It
satellites.evidence: The Odes, Hekuang: 誰謂宋遠？跂予望之 — “who says Song is far? On tiptoe I can see it.” 望 begins as looking toward the far; from there it comes to mean hoping, as in 希望 and 願望.
satellites.caveat: The semantic route from gazing to hoping is the dictionaries’ account.
